1.explanation:
These smoke-test documents cover the core code-annotation feature across multiple scenarios:
- code-annotation.qmd (2022/12/12) provides the initial test case for simple inline annotations.
- code-annote-simple.qmd verifies baseline rendering of annotations.
- code-annote-hover.qmd tests interactive hover annotations.
- code-annote-latex.qmd checks LaTeX output of annotations.
- code-annote-select.qmd examines selection-based annotation rendering.
By comparing these known-good tests with the C/C++ and VHDL cases, you can isolate why annotation markers aren’t being transformed into circled numbers for those languages and reproduce the issue in the test harness.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show that in VHDL and C/C++ code blocks the inline annotation markers “<1>” and “<2>” remain as plain text next to the code rather than being rendered as circled numbers (①, ②). In contrast, R and Python code blocks correctly replace the markers with the numbered circles in the HTML output. The first image shows the VHDL and C++ snippets with raw “<1>”, “<2>” tags, and the second image shows R and Python snippets with proper circled annotations.
